rows.description: A young professional holds tension in the shoulders during deadlines, and stretching or brief breaks help. Colleagues may read tight shoulders as irritation when it is strain.

rows.description: An adult shrugs with palms up to show helplessness or an apology, but if used to dodge responsibility it can feel dismissive. Adding words shows ownership.

rows.subtype: Hands behind the back in respect [Expressing]
rows.description: A young professional stands with hands behind the back in a formal setting or before a senior, showing respect or attentiveness in many cultures. It can seem stiff elsewhere.

rows.description: A young leader spreads the arms wide to invite the team and show openness, though the effect depends on genuine listening.

rows.subtype: Rubbing hands and drumming at work [Mismatch]
rows.description: A colleague rubs the hands in anticipation or drums the fingers in impatience, and it can be either. Asking about it works better than guessing.

rows.subtype: Wringing hands and grief or anxiety [Interpreting]
rows.description: An adult wrings the hands during a hospital wait or hard news, a sign of anxiety or grief. Quiet presence and a calm offer of help matter more than words.

rows.description: A young professional chooses between a handshake, namaste or a nod based on the person and setting, respecting religious and personal preferences. Asking or following the other's lead shows care.

rows.description: An adult places a hand over the heart to thank someone or show sincerity, a widely understood gesture in many places. Its warmth comes from the whole manner, not the gesture alone.

rows.subtype: Finger to lips and safety limits [Mismatch]
rows.description: A young adult reads finger-to-lips as a polite request for quiet in a hospital or as a coaxing secret. If someone uses it to demand secrecy about something that frightens or harms, that is a warning sign; sharing it with a trusted person is right.

rows.description: A young professional uses an open palm to invite a colleague to speak, or a calm hand to slow a heated exchange. Used warmly it shares the floor; used as a sharp stop-signal at seniors it may seem controlling, so tone and status matter.
